amazing-grace.text: These words were first printed in 1779, in Olney Hymns, a hymnbook made in an English village with the poet William Cowper. Their title there was Faith's Review and Expectation.
amazing-grace.source: Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, Hymn 41; Wikipedia, "Olney Hymns"

amazing-grace.text: The tune uses only five different notes, a pentatonic scale. Moved to F sharp major, all five are black keys on a piano.
amazing-grace.source: The tune's own notes (G, A, B, D and E); Wikipedia, "Pentatonic scale"

amazing-grace.text: The tune is called New Britain. Its two halves first appeared in 1831 as two tunes, Gallaher and St. Mary, in Virginia Harmony, a shape-note book whose notes have shapes that show their place in the scale.
The verse about ten thousand years, often sung last, isn't from the 1779 words. It came from an older hymn, and Harriet Beecher Stowe set it with Amazing Grace in Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852).
amazing-grace.source: Wikipedia, "Amazing Grace", on the verses added later
